Packaging · Structural design

A gift box with a second life.

Four fold-out compartments turn a compact dry-fruit gift box into a serving tray.

RolePackaging design
ScopeResearch, structure, dielines, prototypes, visual design
ContextPackaging project

The brief

Make gifting useful beyond the moment

The aim was to create a multifunctional gift box that also works as a display tray. The design brings together presentation, portability, and the practical experience of serving dry fruits.

Research & development

Designing the opening experience

Research looked at premium dried-fruit brands, luxury gifting, and modular packaging. Four compartments fold outward for serving and return inward to make a compact box. An integrated handle supports carrying.

Prototyping

Testing how the structure comes together

The project used paperboard for a lightweight but sturdy structure. Dielines and physical iterations explored the folding mechanism and compartment stability. Purple and gold motifs gave the packaging a celebratory identity.

Outcome

From gift box to a reusable serving format.

One package, two functions: the four-compartment gift box opens into a serving tray and folds back for storage. Dielines and physical prototypes demonstrate the transformation and the integrated carrying handle. This changes the package’s intended use beyond gifting; durability, waste reduction, and user satisfaction were not measured.
